ex_en: Where are you going? (to a man)
What do you want? (to a woman)

note: Libyan possessive particle متاع mtā3 + suffix (also shortened تاعي tā3i). Moroccan ديالي is not Libyan.

ex_en: This is the key of the door.
note: Agrees: متاعت mtā3t (f.) and متاعين mtā3īn (pl.) are also heard.

ex_en: These are my friends from work.

note: Reflexive with روح rū7 'soul' + suffix: روحك rū7ik yourself, روحه rū7a himself.

ex_en: I live alone in the flat.
note: وحدك wa7dik (you alone), وحده wa7da (he alone).

I want to tell you something.
They have known each other for a long time.
They all came to the wedding.
All of us want to go.
The man who came yesterday is my uncle.
note: Invariable relative pronoun for all genders and numbers.
Presentative ها + pronoun: هاك hāk (here you are), هاهو hāhu (there he is).
Presentative راه rā + suffix; more common in western Libya.
Short form شن shin is very common: شن تبي؟
وينها wīnha (where is she?), وينهم wīnhum (where are they?).

ex_en: Shall we go to the beach? Why not!

en: for how much; at what price

note: Also مينو mīnu; شكون shkūn is understood but more Tunisian/Moroccan.

ex_en: Who did you bring the gift for?
What's wrong with you? Are you ill?

note: Mostly eastern Libya; علاش 3lāsh in Tripoli.

ex_en: How old are you, my boy?

note: شنو shinu used with masculine, شني shini with feminine referents.
Contraction of في شنو fi shinu.

ex_en: The book is on the table.
note: Often reduced to عَ 3a before the article.

ex_en: I've just come from the airport.

note: Libyan uses لـ li- for 'to (a place)' where MSA uses إلى.
With suffixes: معاي ma3āy, معاك ma3āk, معاه ma3āh.
عند + suffix is the normal way to say 'to have'.

ex_en: The cat is under the chair.
The keys are on top of the fridge.
I'll wait for you in front of the mosque.
The car is behind the house.
The pharmacy is between the bank and the restaurant.

note: Also لي lī, لمّا lamma in some areas.

ex_en: The shop is in the middle of town.

note: Also an adverb; برا! barra! = get out!

ex_en: The restaurant is opposite the bank.

note: Somewhat formal; دايِر بـ dāyir b- also used.

ex_en: The national team plays against Tunisia.
I got it from my aunt's.
I'll come to you after dinner.

en: for the sake of; because of
ex_en: I did it for your sake.
Take this instead of that one.
Its colour is like the colour of the sky.
note: Understood in Libya, but كيف kīf is more typical.

ex_en: The house is close to the sea.
The airport is far from town.
note: Libyan uses على 3la where MSA uses عن 3an.

ex_en: Do you want tea or coffee?

ex_ar: نبي نجي لكن ما عنديش وقت.
ex_en: I want to come but I don't have time.

ex_en: I didn't come because I was ill.
I was late because the road was jammed.

ex_tr: ana jāy, amma huwa ma na3rafsh.
ex_en: I'm coming; as for him, I don't know.

note: Libyan; from ما يسالش 'it doesn't owe anything'.
Circumfix around the verb: ما مشيتش ma mshītish.
